 Precious metals break to new 52-week lows as us dollar reaches new 19-month high
 By  Gary Wagner 
 Published: Nov 17, 2026 - 1:47 AM Updated: Nov 17, 2026 - 1:53 AM Kitco Commentaries Opinions, Ideas and Markets Talk 
 Featuring views and opinions written by market professionals, not staff journalists.
 (Kitco Commentary) - At the start of the week, gold futures basis the December Comex contract gapped beneath a double bottom that had been tentative support for the precious metal. 
 The double bottom came in at around $3,880, which closely matches recent lows as well as the low hit back on October 28, 2025. Gold opened definitively beneath that level and drifted lower, closing Monday at $3,835 for a loss of $28.60 (0.74%) on the day.
 Silver had also been trading right at a key double bottom at the end of last week, but decisively broke beneath that formation, built from recent lows and the low reached on November 21, 2025, at around $48. Silver gave up substantial ground on Monday, with futures closing lower by $1.74 (3.68%) at $46.93, a new 52-week low.
 A decline in crude oil prices today of roughly 4% should have been supportive of the precious metals; however, it offered little cushion to falling prices in gold and silver.
 The logic for that support is sound. West Texas Intermediate settled near $85.72 and Brent near $92.44 after reports that Washington is not weighing imminent strikes on Iran, and cheaper oil eases the very inflation pressure that has been driving rate hike bets. 
 Treasuries responded as expected, with the 10-year yield slipping about two basis points to 5.12% and the 2-year easing to 4.82%. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh also spoke today but confined his remarks to artificial intelligence, offering no fresh hawkish guidance. Under normal circumstances, lower oil, lower yields and a quiet Fed chair would be the recipe for a bounce.
 The metals fell anyway because the bigger picture has not changed. October consumer prices rose 0.4%, with core up 0.3%, both hotter than forecast, and the CME FedWatch tool now puts the odds of a quarter-point hike at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting above 90%. A two basis point dip in yields does little against that backdrop. 
 The dollar index held near 103.4, its strongest level since April 2025, and a firm dollar raises the cost of gold and silver for every buyer outside the United States. Today’s risk-off tone, led by another slide in technology shares, sent money toward the dollar rather than toward the metals.
 Silver once again took the heavier blow. The gold-silver ratio widened to roughly 82-to-1 from just under 80 on Friday, the pattern we typically see when selling is driven by the dollar and interest rates rather than anything specific to silver. The white metal now trades about 61% below its January record near $121.65.
 Technically, the broken double bottoms now become resistance. Gold must reclaim $3,880 and silver $48 before either chart shows any repair, and until that happens the path of least resistance remains lower, with the round number at $3,800 the next obvious test for gold and no level of technical support until roughly $3,500. 
 The calendar offers several catalysts: October retail sales on Tuesday, the minutes of the Fed’s last meeting on Wednesday, and a full slate of Fed speakers including Waller, Williams and Hammack. A soft retail sales number would give hike odds their first real chance to ease, while a strong one would likely keep the dollar bid and the metals on the defensive. 
 For more daily gold market analysis, visit us at thegoldforecast.com. 
 Wishing you as always, good trading.
 Gary Wagner
